children: Celebrating its tenth edition, the elite list of BW Disrupt 40 Under 40 features winners including the founders of Nothing India, EMotorad, Indo Era, Chalo Mobility, Nykaa, Let’s Try and many more

India’s startup ecosystem has evolved from a small, metro-centric technology community into a significant engine of innovation, employment and enterprise creation. Since the launch of the Startup India initiative in 2016, the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) has recognised more than 2.01 lakh startups, which together have generated over 21 lakh direct jobs.
Nearly 48  per cent  of recognised startups have at least one woman director, highlighting the expanding participation of women entrepreneurs in India’s business landscape.
The ecosystem’s relevance now extends well beyond venture funding and unicorn valuations.

Startups are creating digital public-service layers, building consumer brands, strengthening supply chains, widening access to financial products, digitising healthcare and education, and developing technology for manufacturing, mobility, clean energy and defence. They are also becoming a channel for commercialising innovation, helping India progress from a services-led digital economy towards one with deeper product, research and manufacturing capabilities.

Over the past decade, the startup landscape has broadened geographically and sectorally. Bengaluru remains a major innovation and funding hub, while Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai and emerging Tier-II cities are developing stronger founder, incubator, talent and investor networks.

This expansion has been supported by low-cost digital connectivity, Aadhaar-enabled and mobile-first services, the Unified Payments Interface, cloud infrastructure, a growing base of technical talent, and policy measures aimed at improving ease of doing business, startup recognition and access to capital.

The ecosystem is also closely linked to India’s larger development ambitions. As the country works towards the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, startups can help generate high-productivity employment, improve the competitiveness of small and medium enterprises, build domestic intellectual property and address challenges in areas such as climate resilience, food systems, financial inclusion, healthcare delivery and urban mobility.

Their potential contribution to GDP lies not only in the revenue they generate, but also in productivity gains, exports, formalisation, technology adoption and the creation of new value chains across the economy.

The funding environment in 2025 demonstrated both the resilience and increasing maturity of India’s startup ecosystem. Indian startups collectively raised around USD 11 billion across more than 936 deals during the year, compared with about USD 12 billion across 993 deals in 2024.

While the overall value was lower than the funding peak of 2021, when startups raised approximately USD 42 billion, the current cycle reflects a shift away from valuation-led growth towards disciplined capital deployment, profitability, better governance and clearer paths to scale.

Growth-stage funding rose more than 14 per cent year-on-year to USD 4 billion in 2025, even as late-stage funding declined to about USD 6 billion amid fewer mega-rounds. Seed-stage funding stood at USD 793 million, indicating that investors are writing fewer but more selective early-stage cheques.
At the same time, public-market activity is improving the exit environment: 18 startups made their stock-market debuts in 2025 and raised around Rs 20,000 crore through fresh share issues.

Fintech remained the largest startup-funding category, attracting more than USD 2.5 billion across 120 deals in 2025. Enterprise technology followed with about USD 1.8 billion, while e-commerce raised roughly USD 1.7 billion and recorded the highest number of deals, at 206.

Emerging areas, including artificial intelligence, deeptech and real-estate technology, each received around USD 500 million; healthtech and consumer services drew about USD 700 million each, while cleantech attracted approximately USD 600 million.

The broader private-capital market also remained strong. India attracted USD 60.7 billion through 1,475 PE/VC transactions in 2025, an 8 per cent increase in investment value and a 9 per cent rise in deal volume year-on-year, according to EY.

Financial services, infrastructure, real estate, technology and e-commerce accounted for 72 per cent of total PE/VC investment. Fundraising reached a record USD 23.2 billion, while startup investment volumes grew 19 per cent to 767 transactions, indicating continued institutional confidence despite global uncertainty and valuation caution.

This transition matters for entrepreneurs and business leaders. India’s next phase of startup growth will be shaped by founders who can build durable companies, turn research into products, create sustainable business models and compete in global markets. Recognising such leadership is therefore important: it strengthens the visibility of role models, gives emerging sectors a platform and reflects the diversity of businesses contributing to India’s innovation economy.
To recognise this new generation of business leaders, BW Disrupt, in association with BW Businessworld, organised the tenth edition of the BW Disrupt 40 Under 40 Awards.

The platform honours entrepreneurs and intrapreneurs under the age of 40 who are building disruptive ventures or reshaping established organisations through innovation, strategy and execution. The awardees represent a cross-section of India’s emerging business ecosystem, leaders creating impact in FMCG, technology, fintech, fashion, real estate, mobility, healthcare, artificial intelligence, education, media and entertainment, among other sectors.

As India moves towards its 2047 development goals, such changemaker and innovators will remain critical to building enterprises that combine commercial success with innovation, employment generation and long-term national impact.

This year, BW Disrupt received over 125 nominations spanning diverse sectors including FMCG, mobility, fintech, D2C, AI, and education. After rigorous evaluation, the entries were whittled down to a carefully curated shortlist of 118 nominees who were invited to present before the eminent jury panel.

Each nominee underwent a multi-tier screening and evaluation against a defined set of parameters, major accomplishments, contributions to organisational growth, leadership journey, strategies for scale, sustainability initiatives, as well as their ability to transform weaknesses into strengths. This transparent and merit-driven approach ensured that only the most deserving names emerged as winners.

The prestigious jury comprised some of the most respected names from the world of venture capital, private equity, entrepreneurship, and industry leadership; Annurag Batra, Chairman and Editor-in-Chief, BW Businessworld and Founder, exchange4media Group; Apoorva Sharma    Managing Partner, Stride Ventures; Nikhil Vora, Founder and CEO, Sixth Sense Ventures; Sanjay Mehta    Founder, 100X.VC; Radhesh Kanumury    Managing Partner, Suvan Ventures; Ankur Bansal    Co-Founder, BlackSoil; Jyoti Khetrapal    Executive Director, Centre of Startup Policy; Nikhil Bhandarkar    Founding Partner, Panthera Peak Ventures; Vikram Gupta    Founder and Managing Partner, IvyCap Ventures; Imran Jafar    Executive Director, Gaja Capital; Kushaagra Nandan    Chairman, The Nandan Group; Co-Founder, LNK Energy and Renergy Dynamics.

The evaluation process considers several parameters, including an individual’s professional journey, key achievements, contribution to organisational growth, leadership capability, market impact, strategic vision, innovation, scalability and sustainability. The platform recognises not only startup founders but also leaders within established companies who are driving transformation from within.

This approach places the spotlight on professionals who have converted challenges into opportunities, built differentiated products and services, expanded businesses into new markets, and created meaningful impact for customers, employees and stakeholders.
